key_insight: Raising the barrel filling ratio from 43% to 53% made detonation-sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr coatings denser and more wear-resistant, though with a slightly higher friction coefficient.
engineering_relevance: For wear-critical parts, tuning detonation-spraying fill ratio is a practical way to improve coating integrity and service life under heavy sliding contact.
method: Detonation-sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr coatings at 43% and 53% barrel filling ratios.
Compared microstructure and phase composition using microscopy and X-ray diffraction.
Ran dry ball-on-disc tribology tests at 10 and 15 N and 5 and 10 cm/s.
evidence_signal: The 53% coating showed the lowest wear rate, reaching 1.23 × 10^-4 mm3/(m·N), with denser structure and lower porosity than the 43% coating.
watch_item: Improved wear resistance came with higher friction, so the best fill ratio may depend on whether the application prioritizes low wear, low friction, or both.
paper_title: Effect of Barrel Filling Ratio on the Microstructure, Phase Composition and Tribological Performance of Detonation-Sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr Coatings
